epigraph.quote: Our priorities over the coming quarters will be to strengthen our product capabilities, translate product development into commercial opportunities and ensure disciplined execution.
epigraph.author: Hemango Gupta, Chief Executive Officer, Q2 FY27 call [6]

web_blocks.text: The right operating dashboard is not a single revenue target. It should follow utilization, customer qualification, contracted coverage, project completion, product ramp, working-capital days and the gap between stated capacity and repeatable output. The disclosures below show a mixture of delivered milestones and forward expectations; the HFC-32 project was not yet commissioned in the latest supplied evidence. [1][4][5][6][7]

web_blocks.caption: Operating indicators and current evidence; forward figures remain management or market estimates, not realized outcomes. [1][2][4][5][6][7]
headers: How to interpret / what remains unproven
rows: Sulphuric acid and HF utilization
FY26: 101% sulphuric-acid and 95% HF utilization; record production reported. [1][2]
High core utilization supports operating leverage but leaves reliability, debottlenecking and feedstock availability important.
Specialty fluorides
FY26 capacity 5,000 TPA; utilization 41%. [1][2]
Substantial installed capacity was not yet being used; the later portfolio expansion was described as early-stage commercialization. [4][5][6]
Solar-grade DHF
Two phases commissioned in FY26; the capacity was later debottlenecked from 20,000 to 25,000 TPA; Q2 FY27 call cited 90–95% utilization. [1][2][4][5][6]
Orders were disclosed at about 85% of annual capacity through FY29, but contracted coverage is not the same as collected cash or realized product margin. [1][3]
HFC-32 project

20,000 TPA planned; Q3 FY27 commissioning target. As of September 30, 2026, the company reported about ₹360 crore committed and ₹231 crore spent; management said roughly 90% of work was complete. [1][4][6]
Commissioning, regulatory production framework, customer approvals, stable operation and ramp are still execution milestones. ICRA specifically flags cost/timing and ramp-up as monitorables. [7][10]
New product/R&D pipeline
FY26 annual report: five to eight pipeline products; November 2026 call: 10 products under development across advanced applications. [1][6]
The scope and date differ; neither count is a commercial revenue forecast. Track approvals and repeat sales, not pipeline count alone.
Working capital

FY26 cycle 91 days, eight days better year on year; H1 FY27 inventory and trade payables rose after bulk fluorspar procurement, and the call said 70% of the reported receivables increase was collected in October. [1][2][4][6]
The buffer supports supply continuity but temporarily ties up cash; subsequent normalization and collections need confirmation.

web_blocks.text: The company cites growth in several markets. It estimates Indian fluorochemicals at US$1.9 billion in FY26 and US$2.8 billion in FY31. It also estimates growth in HF, solar-grade DHF and HFC-32. These are market totals, not TANFAC sales forecasts. India’s Kigali schedule also shapes future refrigerant use. [1][2][10][11]

web_blocks.caption: Promise versus delivery: status at the latest date in the supplied evidence. [1][2][3][4][5][6][7]
headers: Evidence of delivery by latest supplied date
rows: Expanded HF unit
Capacity increase from about 14,850 to 30,000 TPA; commissioned October 2024.
Company reports on-time commissioning and FY26 utilization of 95%; this is the clearest completed expansion in the record. [1][2][3]
Solar-grade DHF
Two phases of 10,000 TPA each, then customer orders and ramp.

Both phases commissioned in June/October 2025; by Q2 FY27, capacity had been debottlenecked to 25,000 TPA and management cited 90–95% utilization. Orders to FY29 are disclosed, while product-level profit and shipment details remain undisclosed. [1][2][4][5][6]
HFC-32 and other downstream products
20,000 TPA facility targeted for Q3 FY27 commissioning.
As of the November 3 call, work was described as about 90% complete and commercial production was still upcoming. It is not yet a demonstrated operating or earnings outcome. [1][4][6][7]

web_blocks.text: The latest H1 FY27 operating data counsel against reading revenue growth as margin recovery. Revenue from operations rose 21.2% year on year to ₹417.7 crore, but operating EBITDA margin was 14.4% versus 16.6% in H1 FY26, and PAT was ₹35.9 crore versus ₹36.5 crore. In Q2 alone, revenue grew 36.6% year on year, while management attributed 85–87% of that increase to realization growth and 12–15% to volume growth. The company also reported stable gross profit per tonne in AHF but lower gross-margin percentage as higher realizations enlarged the revenue denominator; new products were still in early ramp. Separate growth in volume, revenue, margins and per-share earnings. [4][5][6]

Follow each project through clear gates. The HF expansion is operating. Solar-grade DHF was commissioned, then debottlenecked. HFC-32 was near completion in September 2026 but had not started commercial production in the latest call. Later HF and solar plans are still proposals. Do not count them as operating capacity. [1][2][4][5][6][7]

web_blocks.caption: Capacity expansion, funding and delivery gates; amounts are company-reported project figures, not equity-market measures. [1][2][3][4][6][7]
rows: HF brownfield expansion
Increase from about 14,850 to 30,000 TPA; company cited approximately ₹100 crore capital cost.
Commissioned in October 2024; management reported on-time execution and FY26 utilization of 95%.
Sustained reliability and economics through a full cycle, not just successful startup. [1][2][3]
Solar-grade DHF
Two initial phases totalling 20,000 TPA; company reported about ₹47 crore funded through internal accruals.
Both phases commissioned in FY26; Q2 FY27 debottleneck raised capacity to 25,000 TPA at nominal incremental capex.
Repeat orders, utilization of the expanded base and disclosed cash/margin contribution. [1][2][4][5][6]
HFC-32 plus associated value-added products
Approximately ₹495 crore announced for the wider facility and associated products; the Q4 call described about ₹405 crore for HFC-32 and ₹90 crore for other value-added products.
By September 30, 2026, the filing showed ₹360 crore committed and ₹231 crore spent; management said about 90% of work was complete. QIP and preferential proceeds were raised during H1 FY27.
Commissioning to schedule and cost, applicable production framework, qualification, stable utilization and cash generation. [1][3][4][6][7]
Further HF / solar-grade expansion
Management later discussed a new HF unit and increasing solar-grade capacity from 25,000 to 50,000 TPA; figures are forward plans.
The November 2026 call described these as priorities for the next phase and discussed a minimum capex expectation, not completed assets.
Formal project approval, funding, schedule, customer coverage and actual construction are not established in the supplied evidence. [6]

web_blocks.text: These rows show a linked process, not separate businesses. Some HF stays inside the plant, and the filings do not show each product’s sales or profit. Read capacity, orders and cash as separate checks. [1][2][6]

web_blocks.caption: Market context cited in company materials. These are external market estimates presented by TANFAC, not company revenue forecasts or calculated market share. [1][2]
rows: Indian fluorochemicals
About US$1.9 billion to US$2.8 billion.
FY26 to FY31; company materials cite third-party market research. [1][2]

About 110 kt to 175 kt.
FY26 to FY31; company presentation estimates roughly 9.7% annual growth. [1][2]

web_blocks.text: Market growth estimates are useful only when linked to the company’s ability to serve the demand. The solar-grade DHF estimate depends on domestic solar-cell manufacturing and its own project pipeline; TANFAC has reported a qualified product and orders for the initial capacity. HFC-32 depends on room-AC and light-commercial cooling demand, but also on the phase-down framework, competition, commissioning and customer approval. The estimates are not a substitute for realized capacity utilization or shipments. A market may grow while a producer’s share, margins or timing disappoint. [1][2][6][10][11]

web_blocks.caption: Management targets and actual status in the latest permitted evidence; guidance is not reclassified as delivery. [1][3][4][5][6][7]
rows: Solar-grade DHF capacity
Initial 20,000 TPA and FY26 order visibility through FY29.
Capacity reported at 25,000 TPA after Q2 FY27 debottlenecking; call cited utilization of 90–95%.
Commissioning and capacity increase delivered; revised contracted coverage after debottleneck was not provided. [1][4][5][6]
HFC-32 facility
Q3 FY27 target, 20,000 TPA and long-term supply arrangements for part of planned capacity.
About 90% construction progress at September 2026; commercial production and qualification were still upcoming.
Project progress is evidence of execution, not evidence of sales, mature utilization or realized margin. [1][3][6][7]
FY27/H2 performance
Management expected stronger H2 performance as new products scaled and input costs moderated.
H1 FY27 revenue rose 21.2%, while operating EBITDA margin was 14.4% versus 16.6% a year earlier and PAT was nearly flat year on year.
The H2 expectation remains forward-looking; the available H1 numbers show operating progress and margin pressure together. [4][5][6]
New product adoption
Annual report disclosed a five-to-eight-product R&D pipeline; later call described 10 products under development.
Q2 FY27 materials say new products were introduced but were in early commercialization and below optimal margin.
Pipeline counts differ by date/scope; measure approvals, repeat orders, stable cost and collections. [1][4][6]

web_blocks.text: Percentages can hide a changing base. Management said most Q2 sales growth came from higher realizations, not volume. It also said AHF gross profit per tonne stayed near stable as price raised the revenue base. These are management explanations; product-level data were not provided. Compare tonnes, sales, gross profit and margin as separate measures. [4][6]

web_blocks.title: Do not treat forecasts as observed KPIs
paragraphs: The Q2 FY27 transcript contains differing utilization expectations for HFC-32 in its answers: one response refers to about 95% utilization in the following year, while another gives 85–90% for the coming financial year. Both are forward-looking and depend on commissioning and stabilization. Preserve that range of management statements rather than selecting one as a realized outcome. [6]

web_blocks.text: On November 3, management raised FY27 revenue-growth guidance from 30% to 35–40%. It also described FY28 growth of 55–60% over FY27 and an EBITDA margin of 24–26% once HFC-32 runs for a full year. These are forecasts, not results. They depend on commissioning, buyer approval, high utilization, stable spreads and new capex. Track sales, tonnes, margin, CFO, receivables and inventory each quarter. If cash does not follow revenue, the growth promise has not yet become an attractive result. [1][4][6]

book_paragraphs: You should audit execution one gate at a time. TANFAC has evidence of delivering the HF expansion and both initial solar-grade DHF phases; the latter also received a nominal-capex debottlenecking that lifted reported capacity to 25,000 tonnes per year by Q2 FY27. The refrigerant project is different: the latest call described substantial progress, but commissioning and customer ramp were still ahead. A target date is not a completion certificate, and a certificate is not yet stable commercial output. [1][2][4][6]

The leading indicators help you distinguish demand from economics. High utilization in sulphuric acid and HF, solar-grade order coverage, qualification progress, product ramp and working-capital discipline are observable. Market TAM figures are only contextual estimates. In H1 FY27, revenue grew faster than PAT and margins remained below the prior-year comparable period; management’s explanation combines input costs, higher realization denominators and initially subdued new-product margins. Keep those causes separate, and test each against subsequent reported utilization, cash conversion and margin data rather than accepting guidance as delivery. [1][4][5][6]

You can turn the expansion narrative into a ledger of gates. The HF unit crossed commissioning and reached a reported 95% utilization in FY26. The solar-grade DHF plant crossed commissioning, secured disclosed order coverage and later gained a debottlenecked capacity increase to 25,000 tonnes. The HFC-32 project had a target date, substantial committed spend and reported construction progress, but the evidence supplied in November still placed it before commercial operation. A plan for still more HF or solar capacity sits one rung earlier. Record the rung for each project, then update only when the next public operating milestone arrives. [1][2][4][6]

Funding and project progress are connected but not identical. The company disclosed a project envelope of approximately ₹495 crore, with management separating HFC-32 and associated value-added products, then reported equity raises during H1 FY27 and substantial project commitment by September. This supports a claim that financing and construction were progressing. It does not tell you the full eventual cost, the time needed to qualify every buyer, or the cash the plant will generate after startup. ICRA specifically names schedule, cost, stabilization and sales ramp as monitoring points. Those are not formalities; they are the operating variables that determine whether capex becomes productive capacity. [1][3][4][6][7]

Use TAM carefully. Company materials cite fast projected growth in Indian fluorochemicals, HF, solar-grade DHF and HFC-32. The demand pools make a strategic rationale plausible, especially where solar manufacturing and cooling capacity are expanding. Yet the market estimate is not TANFAC’s served market, and a projected endpoint is not a booked order. The DHF order book speaks to a defined portion of initial capacity; the HFC project has agreements for a portion of planned output, with regulatory and qualification conditions still relevant. The most useful operating evidence remains shipped product, customer qualification, repeat orders, utilization and cash. [1][2][6][10][11]

Finally, treat management’s promise-versus-delivery record with fairness. The company has shown project execution on the HF expansion and solar-grade DHF phases. It also improved working-capital days in FY26. At the same time, early new products were reported at subdued margins, H1 FY27 margin percentages remained below the prior-year period, and HFC-32 had not yet completed its ramp in the supplied record. Neither blanket skepticism nor automatic acceptance is warranted. You have enough evidence to recognize completed gates and enough open gates to keep the future conditional on delivery. [1][4][5][6][7]

An operating dashboard becomes more valuable when each indicator has a failure interpretation. High utilization in the core may indicate demand and execution, but can also leave little spare capacity for maintenance. An order book may reduce demand uncertainty, but it does not guarantee delivery or collection. A lower margin percentage may partly reflect a larger revenue denominator while absolute gross profit per tonne is stable, as management said for AHF; it may also signal a lag in pass-through or the cost of introducing products. The job is to triangulate utilization, absolute profit, margin percentage, project status and cash conversion, not to select the one indicator that best supports a growth narrative. [1][4][6]

Where management guidance varies, preserve the uncertainty instead of smoothing it away. In the November 2026 call, management offered different utilization expectations for HFC-32 across answers, including a figure around 95% and a range around 85–90% for the following year. That spread is a forecast uncertainty; it is not an actual utilization result. The same principle applies to strong-H2 expectations and market-size forecasts. Later financial results can resolve whether the project started on time, how quickly it stabilized, and whether customer orders translated into volume. Until then, label guidance as management’s current expectation and keep it separate from completed execution. [4][6]

A useful update protocol is to ask one question per reporting period. Was the project commissioned? Did the newly installed line qualify its buyers? What share of capacity operated, and for how many months? Did the product contribute to absolute gross profit, or did only revenue rise with input pass-through? Did the working-capital cycle normalize after precautionary inventory? The supplied sources answer some of these for HF and solar DHF, but not yet for HFC-32. If each new filing is read against the same questions, the narrative can advance only when evidence advances; it will not confuse an announced target with a demonstrated operating result. [1][4][5][6]

Management’s KPI commentary itself identifies reasons to avoid single-cause explanations. Raw-material prices and pass-through timing affect margins; higher realization can lower margin percentage even when gross profit per tonne is described as stable; new products may start at less-than-optimal margins; and higher power, fuel and freight costs were reported in H1 FY27. These drivers may overlap. The next useful evidence is a consistent bridge between revenue, volume, gross profit, operating expense and cash, not a repetition of one factor. The supplied filings do not provide a product-level bridge, so the causal account remains partly at group level. [3][4][5][6]

You and I should now write down the new bar management has set, then refuse to confuse the bar with an achievement. On the November 2026 call, the Managing Director raised FY27 revenue-growth guidance to 35–40% from 30%, and described FY28 growth of 55–60% over FY27 with a 24–26% EBITDA margin as HFC-32 moves into full-year production. That outlook has an operational sequence behind it: finish the plant, commission safely, qualify customer supply, reach utilization, earn the stated margin and collect the cash. If any link slips, the later links move with it. Your scorecard should keep each milestone separate, so one strong revenue quarter cannot be used to declare that the full project economics have arrived. [4][6]

book_callouts.title: Reflection — the evidence ladder
book_callouts.text: For every expansion, what is the latest evidenced gate: announced, funded, under construction, commissioned, qualified, utilized, or profitable? TANFAC’s supplied record reaches different rungs for HF, solar-grade DHF and HFC-32. Do not collapse them into one growth claim. [1][4][6]
